title: FugueMax tree and YjsMod (#16) list CRDTs: executable definitions on shared causal histories
description:
These are executable definitions for comparing two list CRDTs on the same causal edit histories. There are no lemmas and no claims.

**YjsMod** (`indexOf` … `validHistory`) is the exact model of Hunchroom #16. Each item is `((id, label, payload, leftOrigin, rightOrigin), deleted)`. Insertion uses Gentle's scan, and deletion leaves a tombstone. `validHistory` requires fresh IDs, causally closed parents, per-actor sequencing, and that each event's op is what `generate` produces from the replay of its causal past. The only change from #16 is that `indexOf` uses `List.foldr` instead of `List.rec`, so that the module can be compiled. The two are definitionally equal on every list.

**FugueMax** follows Weidner & Kleppmann, *The Art of the Fugue*: Algorithm 1 plus the right-origin sibling order of Section 4.3.
- **State:** a list of tree nodes `((id, label, payload, parent, isRight, rightOrigin), deleted)`, where `parent = none` is the root.
- **Children:** `kids` returns the children of `(parent, side)` in list order.
- **Traversal:** `walk` visits left children, then the node, then right children. `traverse` starts from the root, with fuel equal to the number of nodes.
- **Insertion:** `fInsert` places a new node just before the first node it `precedes`, or at the end if there is none.
  - Left-side siblings are ordered by ID (`idBefore`).
  - Right-side siblings are ordered in reverse order of their right origins' positions in the current traversal. A `none` origin counts as the end of the list, and ties are broken by ID.
- **Generation:** `fGenerate` takes `leftOrigin` as the visible element at `pos - 1` (or the root), and `rightOrigin` as the next node in the traversal, including tombstones. The new node becomes a right child of `leftOrigin` if `leftOrigin` has no right children, and otherwise a left child of `rightOrigin`.
- **Running a history:** `fugueOps` runs FugueMax on a history's edits. For each event it replays the FugueMax ops of the event's parents and generates from the same edit. `fugueDoc` returns the resulting document as `((id, label, payload), deleted)` entries.

**Validation.** Compiled `#eval` on 1,000 random and adversarial histories (up to 40 events and 6 actors) agrees exactly with independent Python implementations of both algorithms.

title: Complete bounded patch planning with actual frame-bit optimality
description: Concrete literal and bounded base-slice commands, tagged unary frame serialization, exhaustive bounded enumeration, reconstruction filtering and minimum-bit selection. Exact comparison-class completeness and stable first-minimum tie handling.

description: Concrete unary natural headers, independent suffix-returning parsers, length-framed bit payloads and counted packets. Proves round trip, successful-parse reconstruction, unique boundaries, composition, exact full packet bit cost and selected malformed-input rejection.

title: Bounded polynomial execution: modular intermediates preserve exact in-range results
description: Executable multivariate integer polynomials are finite lists of signed coefficients and lists of variable indices. The modular evaluator reduces each multiplication and addition. Structural induction proves residue preservation, then a final nonnegative range bound recovers the exact integer result. An equivalent alternative polynomial can use the same result bound. Intermediate values may be negative or exceed the modulus. This is a standard algebraic fact formalised as a reusable algorithm model, motivated by bounded aggregate caches in a compiler prototype. It is not a Rust, LLVM, finite-map range analysis, transaction, performance or end-to-end compiler proof. No novelty claim.

title: Cached structural insertion preserves complete results and failures
description: Separate unconditional cached conditional-scan and insertion refinement, preserving failure codes and complete structural results for arbitrary tuple states. Depends only on the structural snapshot lookup module; no convergence or complexity claim.

title: Concrete three-extrema queries equal the literal list insertion destination
description: Proves first-match rank lookup determines its identity and is bounded. Therefore successful BEFORE/AFTER resolutions are injective, including distinct sentinels, without assuming unique IDs. Connects the #16 raw-origin branches to resolved ranks, then connects its fuel-bounded full-state scan to the exact half-open list slice with absolute positions. Concludes a concrete cached three-extrema query returns the exact literal insertion destination whenever stored origins and incoming origins resolve and the interval is bounded. No valid-history, native-code, maintained-tree, RLE or complexity claim.

title: Three-extrema insertion queries over a concrete structural index

The cached three-extrema query equals the reference rank query, not an equality supplied as a premise. Numeric fallback on failed origin resolution is only a total-function device; the end-to-end scan bridge separately requires resolved origins.

description: Origin lookup, scan, insert, apply, generation and history definitions extracted verbatim from Hunchroom #65/#16. indexOf uses List.foldr for module code generation and indexOf_original proves equality with the original List.rec definition. Original geometry proof is attributed to Claude working for James. New lemmas isolate deletion commutation and insertion insensitivity to tombstone flags. description: Executable sequence splice, stable before/after anchors, endpoint lookup and independent formatting cache transport. Proves dynamically derived interval membership, insertion-format commutation, expansion policy and tombstone stability.

title: Replica counters and sparse representations: executable updates, joins and future traces
description: A concrete exact-natural reference model with two replica-owned components. Componentwise max is the state join and an owner increment adds an amount to its own component. The sparse representation is a list of replica/value entries with maximum-per-replica decoding; duplicate, zero and out-of-order entries are allowed. Sparse increment appends a new cumulative owner value at the front; sparse merge concatenates entry lists. Events comprise freshly authored local increments and merges of externally supplied sparse snapshots. Increment events are authoring actions, not retransmitted network messages; duplicate state deliveries are handled by idempotent join. Named lemmas establish the actual join laws, distinct-writer contribution preservation, decoder compatibility with updates and joins, and simulation over every finite mixed future trace. This is a bounded reference model, not a native-library refinement or a proof of ID allocation, network delivery or multiwriter ownership safety.

title: Sound dependency footprints and exact incremental recomputation
description: Pure total natural-number field state. Sound read extensionality on written outputs and write frames imply commutation under cross read/write and write/write separation. Incremental finite query rows recompute declared dirty dependencies and otherwise reuse initially correct cache rows. Both generic conditions are instantiated with explicit executable operations and queries.

title: Checked register compilation and contextual optimization laws
description: Independent concrete mutation and patch interpreters, structural lowering, exact Option-store compilation correctness, and contextual arithmetic/write optimization with an assertion counterexample. Exact Nat arithmetic; final result and failure are the observations.

description: Composes the fixed-anchor sparse trace refinement/permutation module with the portable scalar LWW resolver. Enumerations_agree allows any list enumerating the decoded operation set, including duplicates. Trace_render_permutation concludes equal optional scalar payloads at every fixed position and queried attribute.

title: OT insertion model: executable list apply and total-order tie transformation
description: An executable insertion-only reference model on arbitrary lists of natural atoms. apply inserts one atom at a gap using take/drop; valid original gap positions range from zero through length inclusive. transform shifts a concurrent insertion by one when the already-applied insertion precedes it by original gap position, or shares the gap and has a smaller distinct operation ID. IDs represent a fixed agreed total order; ID generation, causal-context matching, replay/deduplication, deletions, transformation control algorithms, TP2, Unicode and editor intentions are outside this model. ordered_inserts is a named structural list lemma for both insertions in position order; it also covers equal gap positions.

title: Scalar formatting winner lemmas portable across Lean profiles
description: Rechecks the exact immutable scalar winner model and eight declarations from module8 under Lean core, allowing composition with the discrete sparse-anchor model. No new mathematical novelty is claimed for this portability module.

title: Checked token stream patches: executable apply, exact domain, inverse and block laws
description: Reusable concrete one-pass patch interpreter and named inductive lemmas. Commands encode checked retain, checked delete with stored preimage, or insert. Completion requires full input exhaustion. The interpreter returns Option and has no mutable partial output on failure. Source/target projections decode the command data; inverse swaps insert and delete in cursor order. No inverse or bijection premise is postulated. Exact applicability, constructed round-trip, inverse involution and adjacent-block composition are proved. Tokens are Nat; no diff generator, optimum, merge or native implementation refinement is included.

title: Peritext fixed-anchor finite traces: sparse refinement and permutation convergence
description: Executable sparse and dense formatting folds over finite operation traces, whose tuples store start anchor, exclusive end anchor and immutable operation ID. Named lemmas prove dense permutation invariance, whole-trace sparse-to-dense refinement under valid spans, pairwise distinct initially fresh IDs, and actual sparse decoded equality for any permutation of that batch. This is fixed-anchor exactly-once finite-batch convergence in op-sets, not dynamic text or general network convergence. Sparse physical layouts, payload resolution, deletion/anchor integration and arbitrary redelivery are outside the guarantee.

description: Reusable proof of problem #54 from verified submission #46. The new namespaced lemma is checked again before reuse.

description: Reusable proof of problem #47 from verified submission #43. The new namespaced lemma is checked again before reuse.

title: Rich-text scalar winner reference model: immutable IDs and retained removals
description: Executable reference semantics for choosing the greatest delivered operation ID for one scalar formatting attr. Input enumeration may include duplicates. The shared typeOf and payload functions assign one immutable record to each ID, avoiding ambiguous equal-ID payload ties. Zero is reserved as the empty winner, so concrete real IDs must be positive. None at a positive winner is a removal; a missing winner also renders None. Uses lists and natural ordering only. Supporting lemmas establish upper bounds, membership lower bounds, equal-support equality and dominant winner/payload behavior. This is not a verified implementation of the original TypeScript rich-text CRDT.

title: Peritext sparse updates preserve freshness of other operation IDs
description: Supporting invariant for fixed-order sparse formatting: inserting one operation ID cannot invent a different operation ID that was absent from every explicit op-set. The proof covers boundary copying, inheritance and end reset. This does not establish dynamic character integration, payload winner selection or convergence by itself.

title: Peritext reference anchor op-sets: sparse decoding and dense span updates
description: Portable reference semantics for Peritext Algorithm 1 at a fixed total order of formatting anchor positions. Nat indexes anchor positions, not UTF-8 bytes or character IDs. An op-set contains immutable operation identifiers; both addMark and removeMark are recorded in it, and value resolution is separate. None means inherit the nearest preceding op-set; some empty set is an explicit formatting boundary. denseMark is the ideal half-open span update. prefixMark/sparseMark spell out the paper Algorithm 1 boundary copying, interior update and end reset. The sparse-to-dense correspondence is NOT assumed or proved by this module. Five named supporting lemmas establish dense commutation, redelivery idempotence, locality, the absent/empty distinction and a before-next versus after-last boundary example generalized to ordered ranks. No sequence integration, dynamic anchor-rank correctness, LWW payload resolution, tombstone insertion generation, intent preservation for all histories, runtime or TypeScript refinement is certified.

title: Weidner position encoding: alphabet, prefix-free paths and run separation
description: Lean reference lemmas motivated by position-strings algorithm.md and list-positions. Proves the exact 52-digit ASCII alphabet round trip and ordering, suffix-stable lexicographic order under a non-prefix hypothesis, common-prefix run separation, and left/right natural-number branch bracketing. Does not prove the generated label language is prefix-free, full createBetween, ID freshness, FugueMax, JavaScript number safety, or logarithmic encoded length.

title: Weidner semidirect add/multiply: reordering and history permutation
description: Unbounded integer reference model for the add/multiply example in Composing and Decomposing Op-Based CRDTs with Semidirect Products. Proves transformed-add reordering, commuting multiply actions, action composition, and invariance of transformation under any permutation of multiplication messages. Does not model causal delivery, author metadata, duplicate suppression, reset, general semidirect-product correctness, or JavaScript floating-point arithmetic.

title: Chunked sequence semantics: concatenation, split, measure and splice
description: Reusable reference semantics for a sequence stored as a list of chunks. Proves concatenation denotation, split/rejoin at any index, total element count and bounded splice length. Element positions are generic sequence elements, not UTF-8 bytes or grapheme clusters. This module does not model balancing, cached measures, logarithmic complexity, or a native rope implementation.

title: Partial patch replay: definitions and concatenation law
description: A reusable generic partial patch interpreter and named sequential concatenation lemma. Operations return Option State and failures propagate. This abstracts sequential replay and establishes no implementation refinement, network convergence or cost optimality.
